items: S-waves cannot pass through liquid media—this key characteristic allowed geophysicists to infer that Earth's outer core is liquid.
Richter Scale is logarithmic; an increase of 1 unit in magnitude represents roughly a 32-fold increase in total energy released.
Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) classifies India into 4 seismic zones (Zone II to V); Zone V is the most vulnerable and includes the entire Himalayan belt and North-East India.
P-wave shadow zone exists as a distinct band between 105° and 145° from the epicenter due to refraction at the core-mantle boundary.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The point where energy is released beneath the Earth's surface is called the Focus or Hypocenter, while the point directly above it on the surface is the Epicenter.
Body waves consist of P-waves and S-waves; P-waves pass through solids, liquids, and gases, whereas S-waves travel only through solids.
Surface waves are the last to arrive on the seismograph, travel along the Earth's surface, and cause the maximum structural damage.
The shadow zone for S-waves spans continuously beyond 105° from the epicenter, proving that the Earth's outer core is in a liquid state.
Earthquake magnitude measures total energy released on the logarithmic Richter Scale, whereas intensity measures visible destruction on the Mercalli Scale.
